observations: A large rounded head shape dominates the center, filled with overlapping flat color zones of gold, teal, yellow, red, and purple, with a double-lobed form rising from the top.
Two eyes are each drawn as tight concentric spiral coils in white and gold, with small radiating lines around them; a rectangular mouth area shows short vertical marks resembling teeth.

A dense border of loose gray looping lines runs along all four edges of the gold-brown background, visually separate from the central figure and distinct in color and weight from the multicolored marks inside.
reading: The rounded form holds its ground against a restless interior: spiral eyes pull attention inward while layered color zones—gold, teal, red, purple—push outward in every direction. The tight coils read as intensity or vigilance; the slack gray loops at the edges feel like static held just outside. The face is composed but crowded, as if containing more than it can easily hold.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, immediate title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #160 and nnxyz nnotb #162. Where #160 sets a dense face against black, #161 uses a warm gold field, and #162 shifts to an olive ground with angular framing—three distinct background strategies across three consecutive titles.

connections.reason: Both works center a large face with spiral-coil eyes and a visible tooth row, but #160 builds those features over a black ground with neon-bright lines while #161 uses warm gold, making the mood contrast directly visible.

nnxyz nifty faces #123 also pairs circular spiral eye forms with a tooth-filled mouth on a flat ground, but its teal field and clean line separation contrast with #161's layered color fill and scribbled overdrawing.

lookingQuestion: The gray looping border and the multicolored marks inside the figure use very different line weights and rhythms—what happens to your reading of the face when you track where one zone ends and the other begins?
ambiguities: The double-lobed form at the top of the head could be read as a crown, ears, or a separate overlapping shape; the image does not resolve this clearly.

Title sequence and recorded creation sequence align for this work, but metadata notes gaps and variants exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so consecutive title numbers are not confirmed as consecutive creation events.
